the AKT1-mTOR pathway is a key regulator of oligodendrogenesis and myelination, and that a neuronal program of oligodengocyte precursor recruitment and myelinogenesis is sufficient to trigger myelination.
“A neuronal program dependent on PI(3, 4, 5)P3 triggers oligodendroglial differentiation and myelination.”

the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the development and maintenance of myelinated tracts in the brain.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie myelin formation and maintenance in the central nervous system.
how myelination is initiated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a PI(3, 4, 5)P3 dependent program is sufficient to initiate all steps of myelinogenesis.
the neuronal program is sufficient for the myelination of unmyelinated neurons.
a neuronal PI(3,P4,5P3)-dependent program of oligodentrocyte precursor (OLP) recruitment and myelinating is sufficient to trigger the myelination of the CNS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activation of the AKT–mTOR pathway in neurons is sufficient for the recruitment and differentiation of wild-type oligodandrocyte progenitors, and for the myelination of axons.
a neuronal PI(3)P3-dependent signaling program is sufficient to induce oligodendroglial precursor cells to undergo differentiation and myelinate axons.
a PI3K–AKT1–mTor signaling pathway in cerebellar neurons is sufficient to induce the recruitment of oligodendrogenic cells and myelination of axons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a neuronal program is necessary for myelination to occur.
the molecular trigger of oligodendrogenesis is neuronal, not glial, and is dependent upon PI(3,5)P _{3} signaling.
